Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates prominent central pulmonary arteries (particularly the right interlobar artery), which is a classic radiological sign of pulmonary hypertension resulting from chronic thromboembolic disease. There is no evidence of pleural effusion, diffuse infiltrates, or massive cardiomegaly to support the other options.
